title: OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) packet
summary: OSPF is an interior gateway protocol (IGP) using link-state routing. OSPF packets are carried directly over IP (protocol 89). Common packet types: Hello (1), Database Description (2), Link State Request (3), Link State Update (4), Link State Ack (5). Header: version (1), type (1), packet length (2), router ID (4), area ID (4), checksum (2), auth type (2), authentication (8).

structure.meaning: OSPF version (2 for OSPFv2, 3 for OSPFv3).
1 Hello, 2 Database Description, 3 Link State Request, 4 Link State Update, 5 Link State Ack.
32-bit router identifier (usually the highest IP address or loopback).
Area the packet belongs to (0.0.0.0 = backbone area 0).
Standard IP checksum of the entire packet (excluding authentication field for OSPFv2).
Auth data (password, or MD5 digest + key ID).
Network mask (4), Hello interval (2), Options (1), Router priority (1), Router dead interval (4), Designated Router (4), Backup Designated Router (4), Neighbors (4 each).

ext.example_decoded: OSPF Hello packet: version 2, type 1, length 44, router ID 10.0.0.1, area 0
notes: OSPF uses IP protocol 89 (not TCP or UDP).
OSPF areas reduce LSDB size; area 0 (backbone) connects all areas.
Designated Router (DR) and Backup DR (BDR) are elected on multi-access networks.
Link State Advertisements (LSAs): Type 1 (Router), Type 2 (Network), Type 3 (Summary), Type 4 (ASBR Summary), Type 5 (External), Type 7 (NSSA External).
OSPFv3 (RFC 5340) supports IPv6 and uses link-local addresses.
